name: ses-lockdown
description: Tether Secure Browser v1.8.1 (Windows Hardening, Phase C: adds Alt+Tab/Shift+Alt+Tab/Ctrl+Alt+Tab/Alt+Esc task-switch blocking while the native keyboard-hardening helper (introduced in Phase A+B, below) is ARMED. KeyClassifier.cs gained two rules on top of the existing Windows-key and Ctrl+Esc ones: Tab is swallowed (both edges, mirroring the Windows-key rule's own shape) whenever the event's own KBDLLHOOKSTRUCT.flags LLKHF_ALTDOWN bit is set — covering Alt+Tab, Shift+Alt+Tab, and Ctrl+Alt+Tab uniformly, since Shift/Ctrl being simultaneously held is irrelevant to the rule — and Escape is swallowed on keydown only while Alt is held, mirroring the existing Ctrl+Esc pattern exactly. Alt itself (VK_MENU/VK_LMENU/VK_RMENU) is never swallowed or otherwise touched, so it can never be left 'stuck' if the hook is removed mid-press. No new IPC message, lifecycle state, admin/UAC requirement, registry/Group Policy change, shell replacement, or taskbar/virtual-desktop handling was introduced — the existing single ARM/DISARM hook lifecycle from Phase A+B governs this rule exactly as it already governs the Windows-key and Ctrl+Esc rules.) Previously v1.8.0 (Windows Hardening, Phase A+B — physically validated. Once the student has successfully started a secure exam (the SAME atomic lockdown:activate-secure-exam-lockdown boundary every prior lockdown mechanism already arms from — see main.ts), a new signed, no-admin-manifest, standard-user native helper process (apps/lockdown/native-helper/, .NET 8/C#, self-contained single-file, spawned and owned by Electron, existing only while armed) installs a WH_KEYBOARD_LL low-level keyboard hook that swallows the Left/Right Windows key (both keydown and keyup, together — see KeyboardHook.cs's 'no stuck modifier' note) and Escape while Ctrl is held (Ctrl+Esc), so the Start menu/Task View/Win+D/M/R/E can no longer be reached during an active exam. Ctrl+Alt+Delete is never referenced anywhere in this feature — the Secure Attention Sequence is intercepted by Windows itself before any user-mode hook ever sees it, and remains the one universal OS-level escape, exactly as before. Ordinary window-close (taskbar/system-menu 'Close', not Ctrl+Alt+Delete/Task Manager) is now also intercepted while the exam is ACTIVE (a conditional BrowserWindow 'close' preventDefault, gated on the exact same lockdownLifecycle ACTIVE state the existing before-input-event browser-chrome-shortcut blocking already uses) — recorded via the existing KEYBOARD_SHORTCUT_BLOCKED/CLOSE_WINDOW vocabulary, never a new event type. The helper is armed strictly INSIDE the existing activate-secure-exam-lockdown handler, after every fresh precheck (process/remote-session/display) has already passed and BEFORE any state is flipped — a failed arm fails the WHOLE activation (KEYBOARD_HARDENING_UNAVAILABLE), exactly like every other precheck failure: Windows remains fully normal, nothing is armed, and this is never treated as an integrity event. CRITICAL CORRECTION baked into the design: losing the helper's heartbeat while ACTIVE does NOT call the ordinary lockdownLifecycle restore — display enforcement, remote-session monitoring, and process detection are untouched and keep running; instead a narrow, separate keyboardHardeningRecoveryLogic.ts state machine covers exam content with its own overlay, records a MANUAL_WARNING integrity signal (never called misconduct), and attempts a bounded (2) number of kill-and-respawn recovery cycles before giving up and staying blocked (never silently resuming with reduced security, never auto-healing on its own — only an explicit relaunch/restore clears it). The helper self-terminates the instant its parent process disappears for ANY reason (opens a wait handle on the parent PID at spawn time; Windows itself additionally, unconditionally removes the keyboard hook the moment ANY process holding it exits, hook or no self-exit code) — Electron gone always means Windows returns to normal immediately, with no service, no Job Object, no registry/Group-Policy/Assigned-Access/Shell-Launcher persistence, and no admin elevation anywhere in this feature (per-user NSIS install, unchanged).) Previously v1.7.6 (display-violation UX + question-navigator sync: physical acceptance testing found two remaining issues after v1.7.5. (1) Display recovery defect — HDMI disconnect/topology-transition testing showed correct detection and a correct warning, but on recovery most of the screen stayed covered, requiring a full Windows restart; physical testing isolated this unrecoverable-screen symptom to the separate native display-overlay recovery path (the precise Windows window/compositor failure mechanism was never independently established — detection itself was confirmed correct). Fixed by REMOVING the second, screen-saver-level, non-closable overlay BrowserWindow entirely for active-exam display-policy violations — detection, decision computation (displayEnforcementLogic.ts, unchanged), and event reporting (onEventType, unchanged) all remain fully native/unweakened, but student-facing blocking is now a bounded, renderer-facing status ({state, reason, displayCount} — never EDID/serials/paths/hardware IDs/names) pushed via a new getDisplayEnforcementStatus()/onDisplayEnforcementStateChanged() bridge (see displayEnforcement.ts's Native Display State Bridge), rendered as the exam page's own React/DOM blur+modal (src/lib/displayViolationOverlay.ts in the main repo) that clears automatically — no reload, no Tether restart, no timer reset, no lost answers — the instant native state returns to OK. (2) Question navigator visual lag — the top navigator visibly updated 2-3 seconds AFTER the new question was already on screen, because it always waited on a separate GET .../question-navigator round trip. Fixed with immediate local navigator synchronization: the CURRENT/ANSWERED/SKIPPED tiles and every tile's locked/canNavigate state now update synchronously from save-and-navigate's own response (src/lib/navigatorLocalSync.ts, reusing the existing pure canNavigateToQuestion rule — never approximated), while the existing GET request still runs in the background to reconcile counts/server-only metadata; a monotonic request-generation guard ensures an older, slow-resolving background refresh can never regress a newer one. The save-and-navigate architecture itself, and the navigator's role as a progress display (never a security source of truth), are both unchanged. Previously v1.7.5 (POLICY_NOT_READY P0 fix: physical testing of v1.7.4 found the exam CONTENT page's mount-time effect still unconditionally re-asserted {active:true, ready:false, ...} — a leftover pre-v1.7.4 fail-open-gap cover — which downgraded an already ACTIVE+READY native state from a successful Phase 2 handoff back to POLICY_NOT_READY, producing the same screen-saver-level, non-closable native overlay ('Preparing your secure exam session') with no Recheck/Exit route, requiring a Windows restart. Fixed in three layers: (1) the blind mount-time cover is removed entirely — native lockdown is established before this page is ever navigated to, so there is nothing left to speculatively cover; (2) POLICY_NOT_READY can never construct the native overlay at all, at the overlay-eligibility layer itself (isOverlayEligibleBlockingReason), so no future readiness-gate transition can reintroduce this failure by a different path; (3) a new narrow, read-only IPC method (getSecureClientEnforcementState) lets the content page query the Electron process's own live enforcement state before rendering — if already ACTIVE+READY (the normal Phase 2 handoff) it is preserved; if not (a direct load, reload, or Tether restart that never re-established native lockdown in this process) content is withheld and the student is routed back through tether-launch's own already-tested secure-reactivation handshake, never a speculative cover flag. See docs/tether-preflight-lifecycle-v1.7.5-policy-not-ready.md. Previously v1.7.4 (pre-exam readiness + safe lockdown activation: fixes three confirmed problems — (1) pre-exam remediation was too restrictive (a screen-saver-level always-on-top overlay could obstruct Task Manager during TeamViewer/display remediation); (2) BLOCKED display decisions were mislabelled as genuine additional-display detections (active&&!ready and inconclusive topology queries both showed 'Additional display connected' with no real evidence — see displayEnforcementLogic.ts's DisplayBlockingReason taxonomy); (3) the exam timer/question content could begin before secure-client attestation and native lockdown activation actually completed. New two-phase lifecycle: PHASE 1 PRE-EXAM READINESS runs every mandatory native precheck (prohibited applications, remote session, display topology) with NO strict overlay and NO submission/timer created, showing a calm in-page remediation screen (Task Manager/Alt+Tab/Windows display settings all remain usable) until an explicit 'Begin examination' action; PHASE 2 SECURE ACTIVATION then creates the submission (PREPARING, no timer/content yet), issues/consumes the launch manifest, requires VERIFIED attestation, re-runs a FRESH native check (closing the race where TeamViewer/a display appears between precheck and Begin examination — see main.ts's lockdown:activate-secure-exam-lockdown), activates native lockdown atomically, and only then calls the authoritative POST /api/submissions/[id]/activate (see Submission.activatedAt in the main repo's prisma/schema.prisma) before the timer starts and Question 1 becomes reachable — enforced server-side (src/lib/secureClientActivation.ts), never merely by hiding React content. Previously v1.7.3 (sandboxed-preload hotfix: dist/preload.js is now bundled with esbuild (--bundle --external:electron) instead of plain tsc output, so it no longer contains a relative require("./shared") that the sandboxed Electron preload require() polyfill rejects with 'module not found' — that failure previously aborted the entire preload script BEFORE contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld ran, silently disabling window.sesLockdown (and therefore getDisplayCount, breaking SINGLE_DISPLAY_REQUIRED exams) with no visible error. sandbox:true/contextIsolation:true/nodeIntegration:false are unchanged; the bridge surface exposed to the page is unchanged. See verifyPreloadBundle.ts (build-time regression guard) and sandboxPreloadRuntimeCheck.ts (runtime regression check against the real built preload). Previously v1.7.2 (mid-exam remote-session monitoring: the REMOTE_DESKTOP_SESSION capability is now polled continuously while an exam is ACTIVE, not just at preflight — see remoteSessionMonitor.ts/remoteSessionMonitorLogic.ts — reusing the existing REMOTE_CONTROL_SOFTWARE_DETECTED/PROHIBITED_APPLICATION_CLOSED event model, deduplicated state transitions, and an event-triggered evidence frame; also fixes a latent poll-serialization bug in processDetection.ts where a `.finally()`-wrapped promise's identity could never match its own in-flight guard, silently freezing during-exam process detection at its first scan result for the rest of the exam. Built on v1.7.1's destroyed-window crash fix: restoreLockdownControls/reportAuditFactBestEffort could throw 'Object has been destroyed' when the BrowserWindow's closed event fired, crashing the main process — restoration is now independent of any window and audit reporting is routed through a shared isWindowUsable/runOnWindowBestEffort guard. Built on v1.7.0's Tether Windows Lockdown Hardening v1 — adds a Windows-only process-detection service for known remote-control/debugging/virtualization/screen-capture applications, a remote-session/VM indicator, a main-owned preflight gate and during-exam blocking overlay, an idempotent restoration lifecycle, and materially strengthened Electron hardening: a permission allowlist, denied navigation/window.open/downloads, packaged-build DevTools prevention, rejected unsafe command-line switches, and blocked browser-chrome keyboard shortcuts. See docs/tether-windows-lockdown-hardening-v1.md. v1.4.0 and v1.5.0 were development-only, never distributed.))

scripts.build: tsc -p tsconfig.json && npm run bundle:preload && npm run verify:preload-bundle
scripts.build:helper: dotnet publish native-helper/TetherKeyboardHelper.csproj -c Release -r win-x64 --self-contained true -o native-helper/bin/win-x64
scripts.start: npm run build && npm run build:helper && electron .
scripts.pack: npm run build && npm run build:helper && electron-builder --dir && npm run verify:package
scripts.dist: npm run build && npm run build:helper && electron-builder
scripts.dist:win: npm run build && npm run build:helper && electron-builder --win --dir && npm run embed:icon && electron-builder --win --prepackaged release/win-unpacked && npm run verify:package -- release/win-unpacked
